display: Retired Toronto piano technician (45 years of tuning, regulation and restoration). I restore unwanted upright pianos in my Etobicoke garage and want to give four playable ones to people and groups who will actually play them.

signals.text: I have four restored, playable upright pianos and I want to decide where they go.
I want these pianos to go to people who will play them badly and often, not to a showroom or a resale listing.
I need a truck or van, and a couple of strong people, to move pianos out of the garage in the next few weeks.
I do not know how to choose between the community groups and families who could take the pianos.
Two more uprights need new bass strings and a full re-felt, and I have not found the time or the patience to finish them.
I keep finding good pianos at the kerb or on a skip, and I cannot stop collecting them.
I saw a good Mason & Risch carried out of a church I served for twenty years and put on a skip, and I hated it. I would like places to hear about pianos before they are thrown out.
I need a firm date and a plan for clearing the garage, because the pianos have to be out before early November.
My wife and I disagree about the garage full of pianos, and I need a solution that works for both of us.
I have worked on pianos all my life and I do not know what I will do with my days once the garage is empty.
I am learning to bake sourdough, and the loaves are still bricks.

offers.text: Four restored, playable upright pianos to give away free to community groups, schools, churches or families.
45 years of tuning, regulation and restoration on uprights and grands, from concert halls to church basements to living rooms.
Phone or in-person advice on whether a donated or second-hand piano is worth moving, and what it will cost to make playable.
A tuning visit, or a first check-up, for a piano I place, so it starts life in good condition.
A garage workshop with a bench, a stringing frame and a cabinet of old hammers, felts and keys. Salvaged parts are available for a repair project.
Detailed condition notes on each piano: make, serial number, origin and the work done.
Contacts among former customers, church musicians and music teachers across Toronto.
A trailer hitch, and time to teach someone the basics of piano care and simple repairs.

catchers.hypo: I run a community centre in Scarborough. We have a room, a kids' music program and no piano. Could you help us find one?
catchers.can: Offer one of the four restored uprights free, check the room and the move, and tune it after delivery.
catchers.confirm: Will the piano be kept and played by the group, with no plan to sell it on?

catchers.hypo: My church is replacing its old piano and the pastor wants to throw it out. Is it worth saving?
catchers.can: Assess the instrument and say if it can be restored. If it can, take it into the garage workshop, or advise on how to find it a new home.
catchers.confirm: Is the piano still in the building and not yet disposed of?

catchers.hypo: My granddaughter wants to start learning piano, and we have no instrument. Do you know of a small upright?
catchers.can: Give a small restored upright to a household that will use it, in line with the request from my former customer Mrs. Eng. I decline payment, since I give them away to be played.
catchers.confirm: Is the piano for someone who will learn or practise on it, rather than for decoration or resale?

catchers.hypo: I have a friend with a van and some strong helpers, and I would like to help move pianos for a good cause. Where do I sign up?
catchers.can: Coordinate pickup and delivery of the four pianos with my friend Dmitri, who already helps with heavy lifting, and add your van and crew to the plan.
catchers.confirm: Can you or your helpers lift and move an upright piano safely, with straps and a dolly?

catchers.hypo: I teach music in a school with no budget for instruments. Our piano is beyond repair.
catchers.can: Match a restored upright to the school and help the teacher with basic care. I can also ask my contacts among music teachers to see who else needs one.
catchers.confirm: Will the piano stay with the school and be used by students?

catchers.hypo: I am a retired woodworker or tinkerer and I want a project. Can I learn piano repair from you?
catchers.can: Show you how to re-felt, re-string and regulate an upright. Two pianos in the garage still need that work, and I want company on them.
catchers.confirm: Are you willing to spend whole days at a workbench in Etobicoke on slow, detailed work?

catchers.hypo: Our building manager is clearing out a basement and there are old pianos. Should we call a junk removal company?
catchers.can: Look at the pianos before they go, identify ones worth saving, and place or take them. Please call before the junk company does.
catchers.confirm: Are the pianos still in place and available for someone to inspect?

catchers.hypo: I'm in Ottawa and run a small music program. Could your daughter help us hear about pianos that need homes?
catchers.can: Ask my daughter Karen, who lives in Ottawa, if she knows groups there that could use an instrument, and ask her to pass on an introduction.
catchers.confirm: Is the program in the Ottawa area, with someone local who can receive and move a piano?

forbids.text: I do not sell the pianos; they are gifts to be played.
I will not give a piano to anyone who plans to resell it.
I cannot lift or load pianos on my own, so moves need a crew, a truck and straps.
I work in the Greater Toronto Area and cannot deliver far outside it.

projects.name: The garage pianos
projects.text: Six donated uprights and a spinet frame in my garage. Four play now and I want to place them with community groups. Two need new bass strings and re-felting.
roles_needed: community group or school to receive a piano
van or truck owner with a crew
apprentice or volunteer to help with re-felting and re-stringing
music teacher to advise on placement

policy.t1: When there is a real prospect, I will give the number of pianos, their makes, the condition of each, my moving needs and my contacts among teachers and church musicians.
policy.t2: When I trust the other party and the match looks strong, I will share the time pressure on clearing the garage and the situation at home behind it.
policy.never: I will never share health details, or anything about my family's finances.
